record.original_question: Give a ``TCS-style'' analysis of MR$^3$ which proves its correctness and convergence under easily verifiable conditions on the input.

evidence.quote: Give a ``TCS-style'' analysis of MR$^3$ which proves its correctness and convergence under easily verifiable conditions on the input.

artifact.status_search_result: Dhillon and Parlett (2004) gave a correctness proof of MR^3 conditional on three internal "requirements" on each representation; Willems and Lang (SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 2013) developed a modular framework reducing correctness to five interface conditions between the core algorithm and its subcomponents. These conditions are monitorable at runtime but are not yet stated as easily verifiable a priori conditions on the input matrix T alone, so a fully "TCS-style" input-side analysis remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: A Framework for the MR^3 Algorithm: Theory and Implementation
status_evidence.snippet: The proof is based on five requirements concerning the interplay between the core algorithm and its subcomponents... these requirements expose quantities that can and should be monitored at runtime.
status_evidence.claim: Correctness has been established conditional on internal requirements that are monitored at runtime, not on a priori input conditions.

status_evidence.title: Multiple representations to compute orthogonal eigenvectors of symmetric tridiagonal matrices
status_evidence.snippet: If each representation satisfies three prescribed conditions then the computed eigenvectors are orthogonal to working accuracy and have small residual norms.
status_evidence.claim: Original correctness analysis depends on conditions imposed on each representation in the tree rather than directly on the input.
